text: REST APIs are a popular way for applications to communicate over the internet. When you design one, you should create clear endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Each request should return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API without confusion. It is also important to use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing clients. Following these best practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and improve over time.
